new_statements.relation_note: Same p.88 sentence: Kamoro and Citak Asmat tonal, rest of Asmat-Kamoro without tonal prosody; no stress statement.
new_statements.identity_note: group-level 'Citak Asmat are tonal'; P&H file Tamnim Citak in that subgroup, but Usher & Suter 2020:153 note Ethnologue's Tamnim Citak sits on the territory of Voorhoeve's Sokoni dialect of Central Asmat and is Citak by self-identification, so whether the tonal remark applies is doubly uncertain. This work is already in round 1's tamn1235 list (no statement was taken from it); recorded here only because the file is now confirmed held by the project with the exact sentence. sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1980. The Asmat Languages of Irian Jaya. Pacific Linguistics B-64. Canberra: ANU. x+177 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 3.1.2.3 p. 22: 'Stress and pitch phenomena have only been studied in the KW dialect' (Central Asmat); sec. 5.2 p. 37 (Citak, Senggo, after Bromley): bisyllables contrastive stress, monosyllables three pitch patterns; sec. 7.2 p. 43: stress/pitch studied only in KW and CI. Tamanim (village 68) appears only in the Citak village list; postscript point 6 p. 123 says Tamanim is NOT Citak-speaking, probably KP or SO dialect of Central Asmat; Yinak/Wooi = Sokoni dialect (sec. 3.3.4 p. 29, wordlists only). Nothing on stress for the Tamanim/Sokoni communalects.
